title: Funds management: Discretionary powers
subject: This guide explains ASIC's approach to exercising its exemption and modification powers to grant individual relief from requirements under the Corporations Act and the Corporations (Passport) Rules 2018 for managed investment schemes and Australian passport funds. It also covers common situations where relief has been granted and when schemes are considered closely related for aggregation purposes.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and the Corporations (Passport) Rules 2018, providing guidance to operators of registered managed investment schemes, corporate collective investment vehicles, passport funds, and their service providers and advisers. It aims to clarify ASIC's discretionary powers and the circumstances in which relief may be granted.
ruling: ASIC will consider individual relief applications on a case-by-case basis, guided by the principles in RG 51 Applications for relief. The guide outlines specific scenarios where ASIC is likely to grant relief, such as for hardship withdrawals, frozen funds, and closely related schemes. ASIC interprets the law to require that relief must not undermine investor protection or market integrity. The guide also sets out when ASIC will aggregate schemes for determining small scheme exemptions. ASIC expects applicants to demonstrate that relief is necessary and that alternative compliance measures are not reasonably available.
